CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Garut Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Garut. 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of regional government administration. 5. Regency Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regency DPRD in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Regency region. 6. Protection is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and children victims of violence and discrimination starting from prevention efforts, services and social rehabilitation. 7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 8. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 9. Protection of Children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of freedom unlawfully. 11. Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 12. Violence against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 13. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development. 14. Domestic Violence hereinafter referred to as KDRT is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion, or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household. 15. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 16. Guardian is a person or body who in fact exercises parental authority as a Parent over a Child. 17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 18. Community is individuals, families, groups, and/or community organizations. 19. Non-Governmental Organization, hereinafter referred to as LSM, is an organization/institution formed by citizens of the Republic of Indonesia voluntarily of their own will and interested in and engaged in the field of social welfare business established by the organization/institution as a manifestation of community participation in efforts to improve community welfare that emphasizes voluntary service. 20. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs in the Garut Regency area. 21. Prevention is an effort to develop the capacity and mechanisms of the Regional Government and community in creating conditions that can prevent the occurrence of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation and/or neglect. 22. Handling is action that includes identification, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of women and children who are victims of acts of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation, maltreatment or neglect. 23. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 24. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing of the impending, ongoing or having occurred violence against victims. 25. Assistance is an effort made by a person or representative from an institution that has expertise in assisting victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 26. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society. 27. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out social functions properly. 28. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 29. Legal Aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to conduct the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender sensitive. 30.

In the event that parents, guardians and/or family as referred to in paragraph (1) do not exist or their whereabouts are unknown or due to a certain reason cannot carry out their obligations and responsibilities, then the obligations and responsibilities may be transferred to the Regional Government and other family members implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER VII

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM VIOLENCE

Article 7

1. Physical violence as referred to in Article 6 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death of women and/or children.
2. Psychological violence as referred to in Article 6 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering to women and/or children.
3. Sexual violence as referred to in Article 6 letter c, includes:
a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:
1\. physical harassment;
2\. verbal harassment;
3\. gestural harassment;
4\. written or pictorial harassment; and
5\. psychological/emotional harassment.
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/ord. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
4. Neglect as referred to in Article 6 letter d, includes:
a. acts that result in the failure to fulfill the needs of children properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after children as they should be, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/or
c. acts of deliberately neglecting women within their household sphere, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
5. Exploitation as referred to in Article 6 letter e, includes:
a. acts of economic or sexual exploitation with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the victim's consent which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or indecent acts.
6. Other violence as referred to in Article 6 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
7. Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
8. Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person/victim is made to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 39

1. Reporting on the implementation of protection for women and children from violence is carried out by:
a. P2TP2A to the Regent;
b. Task Force for the Protection of Women and Children at the Sub-District Level to the Sub-District Head; and
c. Task Unit for the Protection of Women and Children at the Village/Sub-District Level to the Village Head/Sub-District Head.
2. Reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be submitted in writing, covering:
a. administration;
b. finance;
c. services; and
d. performance.
3. Submission of written reports as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out at least once every 3 (three) months.

CHAPTER XII

SANCTIONS

Article 41

1. Any person who intentionally fails to provide protection for women and children resulting in the occurrence of violence, allows violence to occur, and/or does not report and does not provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in the applicable laws and regulations.
2. Regency Regional Apparatus that have the duties and functions of administering protection, failing to carry out their obligations and responsibilities shall be subject to administrative sanctions.
3. Management of P2TP2A, Task Force for the Protection of Women and Children at the Sub-District Level, Task Unit for the Protection of Women and Children at the Village/Sub-District Level and other institutions or organizations in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations that carry out protection duties, if they violate protection principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the mechanisms applicable within the internal institutions or respective organizations.

Article 3

The purpose of regulating the protection of women and children from acts of violence is to provide guidance and direction for the Regional Government and community in conducting prevention, services and social rehabilitation of women and child victims of acts of violence.

Article 36

1. The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector, NGOs/social organizations concerned with women and children in the protection of women and children against acts of violence.
2. The partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through:
a. notification of information on employment opportunities for women victims of violence;
b. education and training for women and children victims of violence;
c. educational assistance for women and children victims of violence who have been withdrawn from their education; and
d. fostering and enhancing the economic independence of women victims of violence.
3. The partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be set forth in the form of an agreement in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Garut Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Garut. 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of regional government administration. 5. Regency Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regency DPRD in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Regency region. 6. Protection is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and children victims of violence and discrimination starting from prevention efforts, services and social rehabilitation. 7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 8. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 9. Protection of Children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of freedom unlawfully. 11. Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 12. Violence against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 13. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development. 14. Domestic Violence hereinafter referred to as KDRT is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion, or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household. 15. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 16. Guardian is a person or body who in fact exercises parental authority as a Parent over a Child. 17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 18. Community is individuals, families, groups, and/or community organizations. 19. Non-Governmental Organization, hereinafter referred to as LSM, is an organization/institution formed by citizens of the Republic of Indonesia voluntarily of their own will and interested in and engaged in the field of social welfare business established by the organization/institution as a manifestation of community participation in efforts to improve community welfare that emphasizes voluntary service. 20. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs in the Garut Regency area. 21. Prevention is an effort to develop the capacity and mechanisms of the Regional Government and community in creating conditions that can prevent the occurrence of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation and/or neglect. 22. Handling is action that includes identification, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of women and children who are victims of acts of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation, maltreatment or neglect. 23. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 24. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing of the impending, ongoing or having occurred violence against victims. 25. Assistance is an effort made by a person or representative from an institution that has expertise in assisting victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 26. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society. 27. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out social functions properly. 28. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 29. Legal Aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to conduct the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender sensitive. 30.

CHAPTER XII

SANCTIONS

Article 41

1. Any person who intentionally fails to provide protection for women and children resulting in the occurrence of violence, allows violence to occur, and/or does not report and does not provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in the applicable laws and regulations.
2. Regency Regional Apparatus that have the duties and functions of administering protection, failing to carry out their obligations and responsibilities shall be subject to administrative sanctions.
3. Management of P2TP2A, Task Force for the Protection of Women and Children at the Sub-District Level, Task Unit for the Protection of Women and Children at the Village/Sub-District Level and other institutions or organizations in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations that carry out protection duties, if they violate protection principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the mechanisms applicable within the internal institutions or respective organizations.

Article 36

1. The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector, NGOs/social organizations concerned with women and children in the protection of women and children against acts of violence.
2. The partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through:
a. notification of information on employment opportunities for women victims of violence;
b. education and training for women and children victims of violence;
c. educational assistance for women and children victims of violence who have been withdrawn from their education; and
d. fostering and enhancing the economic independence of women victims of violence.
3. The partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be set forth in the form of an agreement in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 7

1. Physical violence as referred to in Article 6 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death of women and/or children.
2. Psychological violence as referred to in Article 6 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering to women and/or children.
3. Sexual violence as referred to in Article 6 letter c, includes:
a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:
1\. physical harassment;
2\. verbal harassment;
3\. gestural harassment;
4\. written or pictorial harassment; and
5\. psychological/emotional harassment.
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/ord. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
4. Neglect as referred to in Article 6 letter d, includes:
a. acts that result in the failure to fulfill the needs of children properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after children as they should be, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/or
c. acts of deliberately neglecting women within their household sphere, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
5. Exploitation as referred to in Article 6 letter e, includes:
a. acts of economic or sexual exploitation with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the victim's consent which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or indecent acts.
6. Other violence as referred to in Article 6 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
7. Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
8. Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person/victim is made to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 3

The purpose of regulating the protection of women and children from acts of violence is to provide guidance and direction for the Regional Government and community in conducting prevention, services and social rehabilitation of women and child victims of acts of violence.

Article 13

1. The community as referred to in Article 10 letter c has the obligation and responsibility for the protection of women and children through community participation activities in the protection of women and children.
2. Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), include:
a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or the competent authorities; and
c. participating in the handling of victims of acts of violence.

Article 26

1. Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 15 letter c constitutes services provided by companions to restore the traumatic condition of victims.
2. Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by:
a. providing guidance and counseling to victims and parents of victims;
b. psychological recovery of victims;
c. accompanying victims and parents of victims in the family and community environment; and
d. providing safe houses for victims of violence who require continuous handling.
3. Special social rehabilitation for women victims of domestic violence and trafficking in persons is carried out by:
a. providing guidance and counseling;
b. psychological recovery of victims; and
c. accompanying victims in the family and community environment.
4. Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented by the Regency Regional Apparatus having main duties and functions in the fields of:
a. social affairs;
b. women's empowerment and child protection;
c. health; and
d. mental and spiritual.
5. In addition to being implemented by the Regency Regional Apparatus as referred to in paragraph (4), social rehabilitation may also be implemented by the community or social service institutions.

NUMBER 13 OF 2016

CONCERNING

BY THE GRACE OF GOD ALMIGHTY

THE REGENT OF GARUT,

Considering:

a. that in order to guarantee and protect the rights of women and children so that they can participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence, it is necessary to undertake efforts to protect women and children optimally through increasing broad community participation; b. that the prevalence of cases of violence against women and children in Garut Regency requires handling and concrete action from the Regional Government to formulate policies and programs to eliminate all forms of violence against women and children; c. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a and letter b, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children from Violence; In View of:

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Garut Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Garut. 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of regional government administration. 5. Regency Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regency DPRD in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Regency region. 6. Protection is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and children victims of violence and discrimination starting from prevention efforts, services and social rehabilitation. 7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 8. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 9. Protection of Children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of freedom unlawfully. 11. Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 12. Violence against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 13. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development. 14. Domestic Violence hereinafter referred to as KDRT is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion, or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household. 15. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 16. Guardian is a person or body who in fact exercises parental authority as a Parent over a Child. 17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 18. Community is individuals, families, groups, and/or community organizations. 19. Non-Governmental Organization, hereinafter referred to as LSM, is an organization/institution formed by citizens of the Republic of Indonesia voluntarily of their own will and interested in and engaged in the field of social welfare business established by the organization/institution as a manifestation of community participation in efforts to improve community welfare that emphasizes voluntary service. 20. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs in the Garut Regency area. 21. Prevention is an effort to develop the capacity and mechanisms of the Regional Government and community in creating conditions that can prevent the occurrence of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation and/or neglect. 22. Handling is action that includes identification, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of women and children who are victims of acts of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation, maltreatment or neglect. 23. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 24. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing of the impending, ongoing or having occurred violence against victims. 25. Assistance is an effort made by a person or representative from an institution that has expertise in assisting victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 26. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society. 27. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out social functions properly. 28. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 29. Legal Aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to conduct the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender sensitive. 30.

Article 26

1. Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 15 letter c constitutes services provided by companions to restore the traumatic condition of victims.
2. Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by:
a. providing guidance and counseling to victims and parents of victims;
b. psychological recovery of victims;
c. accompanying victims and parents of victims in the family and community environment; and
d. providing safe houses for victims of violence who require continuous handling.
3. Special social rehabilitation for women victims of domestic violence and trafficking in persons is carried out by:
a. providing guidance and counseling;
b. psychological recovery of victims; and
c. accompanying victims in the family and community environment.
4. Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented by the Regency Regional Apparatus having main duties and functions in the fields of:
a. social affairs;
b. women's empowerment and child protection;
c. health; and
d. mental and spiritual.
5. In addition to being implemented by the Regency Regional Apparatus as referred to in paragraph (4), social rehabilitation may also be implemented by the community or social service institutions.

Article 36

1. The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector, NGOs/social organizations concerned with women and children in the protection of women and children against acts of violence.
2. The partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through:
a. notification of information on employment opportunities for women victims of violence;
b. education and training for women and children victims of violence;
c. educational assistance for women and children victims of violence who have been withdrawn from their education; and
d. fostering and enhancing the economic independence of women victims of violence.
3. The partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be set forth in the form of an agreement in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

b. accompanying victims at the investigation, prosecution, and examination levels in court hearings and helping victims to fully explain the violence they experienced; and
c. coordinating with fellow law enforcers, volunteer assistants, and social workers so that the judicial process proceeds as it should.

Article 7

1. Physical violence as referred to in Article 6 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death of women and/or children.
2. Psychological violence as referred to in Article 6 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering to women and/or children.
3. Sexual violence as referred to in Article 6 letter c, includes:
a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:
1\. physical harassment;
2\. verbal harassment;
3\. gestural harassment;
4\. written or pictorial harassment; and
5\. psychological/emotional harassment.
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/ord. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
4. Neglect as referred to in Article 6 letter d, includes:
a. acts that result in the failure to fulfill the needs of children properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after children as they should be, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/or
c. acts of deliberately neglecting women within their household sphere, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
5. Exploitation as referred to in Article 6 letter e, includes:
a. acts of economic or sexual exploitation with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the victim's consent which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or indecent acts.
6. Other violence as referred to in Article 6 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
7. Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
8. Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person/victim is made to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Protection is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and children victims of violence and discrimination starting from prevention efforts, services and social rehabilitation. 7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 8. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 9. Protection of Children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of freedom unlawfully. 11. Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 12. Violence against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 13. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development. 14. Domestic Violence hereinafter referred to as KDRT is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion, or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household. 15. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 16. Guardian is a person or body who in fact exercises parental authority as a Parent over a Child. 17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 18. Community is individuals, families, groups, and/or community organizations. 19. Non-Governmental Organization, hereinafter referred to as LSM, is an organization/institution formed by citizens of the Republic of Indonesia voluntarily of their own will and interested in and engaged in the field of social welfare business established by the organization/institution as a manifestation of community participation in efforts to improve community welfare that emphasizes voluntary service. 20. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing of the impending, ongoing or having occurred violence against victims. 25. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out social functions properly. 28. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 29. Legal Aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to conduct the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender sensitive. 30.

Article 1

Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 8. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 9. Protection of Children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 10. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development. 14. Guardian is a person or body who in fact exercises parental authority as a Parent over a Child. 17. CHAPTER XII

SANCTIONS

Article 41

1. Any person who intentionally fails to provide protection for women and children resulting in the occurrence of violence, allows violence to occur, and/or does not report and does not provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in the applicable laws and regulations.
2. Regency Regional Apparatus that have the duties and functions of administering protection, failing to carry out their obligations and responsibilities shall be subject to administrative sanctions.
3. Management of P2TP2A, Task Force for the Protection of Women and Children at the Sub-District Level, Task Unit for the Protection of Women and Children at the Village/Sub-District Level and other institutions or organizations in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations that carry out protection duties, if they violate protection principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the mechanisms applicable within the internal institutions or respective organizations.

Article 7

1. Physical violence as referred to in Article 6 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death of women and/or children.
2. Psychological violence as referred to in Article 6 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering to women and/or children.
3. Sexual violence as referred to in Article 6 letter c, includes:
a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:
1\. physical harassment;
2\. verbal harassment;
3\. gestural harassment;
4\. written or pictorial harassment; and
5\. psychological/emotional harassment.
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/ord. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
4. Neglect as referred to in Article 6 letter d, includes:
a. acts that result in the failure to fulfill the needs of children properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after children as they should be, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/or
c. acts of deliberately neglecting women within their household sphere, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
5. Exploitation as referred to in Article 6 letter e, includes:
a. acts of economic or sexual exploitation with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the victim's consent which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or indecent acts.
6. Other violence as referred to in Article 6 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
7. Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
8. Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person/victim is made to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 11

1. The Regional Government as referred to in Article 10 letter a, is obliged and responsible to:
a. formulate and implement programs and activities related to the protection of women and children;
b. implement protection of women and children from violence;
c. supervise services to victims of violence based on minimum service standards in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations; and
d. allocate budget for protection of women and children from violence according to regional financial capacity.
2. In order to carry out the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regional Government formulates programs and activities for the protection of women and children in a regional action plan which is part of the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan

Article 36

1. The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector, NGOs/social organizations concerned with women and children in the protection of women and children against acts of violence.
2. The partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through:
a. notification of information on employment opportunities for women victims of violence;
b. education and training for women and children victims of violence;
c. educational assistance for women and children victims of violence who have been withdrawn from their education; and
d. fostering and enhancing the economic independence of women victims of violence.
3. The partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be set forth in the form of an agreement in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 7

1. Physical violence as referred to in Article 6 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death of women and/or children.
2. Psychological violence as referred to in Article 6 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering to women and/or children.
3. Sexual violence as referred to in Article 6 letter c, includes:
a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:
1\. physical harassment;
2\. verbal harassment;
3\. gestural harassment;
4\. written or pictorial harassment; and
5\. psychological/emotional harassment.
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/ord. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
4. Neglect as referred to in Article 6 letter d, includes:
a. acts that result in the failure to fulfill the needs of children properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after children as they should be, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/or
c. acts of deliberately neglecting women within their household sphere, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
5. Exploitation as referred to in Article 6 letter e, includes:
a. acts of economic or sexual exploitation with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the victim's consent which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or indecent acts.
6. Other violence as referred to in Article 6 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
7. Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
8. Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person/victim is made to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 8. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 9. Protection of Children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of freedom unlawfully. 11. Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 12. Violence against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 13. Article 17

Services as referred to in Article 15 letter b, take into account:
a. service principles; and
b. forms of services to victims.

Article 22

Health services as referred to in Article 19 letter a number 3 include:
a. first aid to victims by competent officers;
b. treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical and paramedical personnel; and
c. referral to health services as needed.

Article 23

1. Legal aid services as referred to in Article 19 letter a number 4 are to assist victims in undergoing the judicial process.
2. Legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by:
a. providing legal consultation that includes information regarding the rights of victims and the judicial process;
b. accompanying victims at the investigation, prosecution, and examination levels in court hearings and helping victims to fully explain the violence they experienced; and
c. coordinating with fellow law enforcers, volunteer assistants, and social workers so that the judicial process proceeds as it should.

Article 11

1. The Regional Government as referred to in Article 10 letter a, is obliged and responsible to:
a. formulate and implement programs and activities related to the protection of women and children;
b. implement protection of women and children from violence;
c. supervise services to victims of violence based on minimum service standards in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations; and
d. allocate budget for protection of women and children from violence according to regional financial capacity.
2. In order to carry out the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regional Government formulates programs and activities for the protection of women and children in a regional action plan which is part of the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan

Article 7

1. Physical violence as referred to in Article 6 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death of women and/or children.
2. Psychological violence as referred to in Article 6 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering to women and/or children.
3. Sexual violence as referred to in Article 6 letter c, includes:
a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:
1\. physical harassment;
2\. verbal harassment;
3\. gestural harassment;
4\. written or pictorial harassment; and
5\. psychological/emotional harassment.
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/ord. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
4. Neglect as referred to in Article 6 letter d, includes:
a. acts that result in the failure to fulfill the needs of children properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after children as they should be, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/or
c. acts of deliberately neglecting women within their household sphere, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
5. Exploitation as referred to in Article 6 letter e, includes:
a. acts of economic or sexual exploitation with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the victim's consent which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or indecent acts.
6. Other violence as referred to in Article 6 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
7. Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
8. Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person/victim is made to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 24

1. Repatriation and social reintegration services as referred to in Article 19 letter a number 5 are carried out to return victims to their families and social environment.
2. Repatriation and social reintegration services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by the Regional Government in coordination with:
a. Regency/City Governments within one Provincial area or outside the Province; and/or
b. related agencies and institutions both Government and non-Government.

Article 3

The purpose of regulating the protection of women and children from acts of violence is to provide guidance and direction for the Regional Government and community in conducting prevention, services and social rehabilitation of women and child victims of acts of violence.

Article 12

1. The Village Government as referred to in Article 10 letter b, is obliged and responsible to:
a. formulate and implement programs and activities related to the protection of women and children;
b. implement protection of women and children from violence;
c. supervise services to victims of violence based on minimum service standards in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations; and
d. allocate budget for protection of women and children from violence according to village financial capacity.
2. In order to carry out the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in paragraph (1), the Village Government formulates programs and activities for the protection of women and children in a Village action plan which is part of the Village Medium-Term Development Plan (RPJMDes).

Article 14

1. Parents, guardians and/or family as referred to in Article 10 letter d legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence, report when violence occurs and protect victims.
2. In the event that parents, guardians and/or family as referred to in paragraph (1) do not exist or their whereabouts are unknown or due to a certain reason cannot carry out their obligations and responsibilities, then the obligations and responsibilities may be transferred to the Regional Government and other family members implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

REGIONAL REGULATION OF GARUT REGENCY

NUMBER 13 OF 2016

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM VIOLENCE

BY THE GRACE OF GOD ALMIGHTY

THE REGENT OF GARUT,

Considering:

a. that in order to guarantee and protect the rights of women and children so that they can participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence, it is necessary to undertake efforts to protect women and children optimally through increasing broad community participation; b. that the prevalence of cases of violence against women and children in Garut Regency requires handling and concrete action from the Regional Government to formulate policies and programs to eliminate all forms of violence against women and children; c. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a and letter b, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children from Violence; In View of:

1. Article 18 paragraph (6) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia; 2. Law Number 17 of 2003 concerning State Finance (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2003 Number 47, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4286); 7. Article 7

1. Physical violence as referred to in Article 6 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death of women and/or children.
2. Psychological violence as referred to in Article 6 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering to women and/or children.
3. Sexual violence as referred to in Article 6 letter c, includes:
a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:
1\. physical harassment;
2\. verbal harassment;
3\. gestural harassment;
4\. written or pictorial harassment; and
5\. psychological/emotional harassment.
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/ord. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
4. Neglect as referred to in Article 6 letter d, includes:
a. acts that result in the failure to fulfill the needs of children properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after children as they should be, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/or
c. acts of deliberately neglecting women within their household sphere, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
5. Exploitation as referred to in Article 6 letter e, includes:
a. acts of economic or sexual exploitation with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the victim's consent which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or indecent acts.
6. Other violence as referred to in Article 6 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
7. Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
8. Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person/victim is made to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 26

1. Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 15 letter c constitutes services provided by companions to restore the traumatic condition of victims.
2. Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by:
a. providing guidance and counseling to victims and parents of victims;
b. psychological recovery of victims;
c. accompanying victims and parents of victims in the family and community environment; and
d. providing safe houses for victims of violence who require continuous handling.
3. Special social rehabilitation for women victims of domestic violence and trafficking in persons is carried out by:
a. providing guidance and counseling;
b. psychological recovery of victims; and
c. accompanying victims in the family and community environment.
4. Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented by the Regency Regional Apparatus having main duties and functions in the fields of:
a. social affairs;
b. women's empowerment and child protection;
c. health; and

SANCTIONS

Article 41

1. Any person who intentionally fails to provide protection for women and children resulting in the occurrence of violence, allows violence to occur, and/or does not report and does not provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in the applicable laws and regulations.

3. Management of P2TP2A, Task Force for the Protection of Women and Children at the Sub-District Level, Task Unit for the Protection of Women and Children at the Village/Sub-District Level and other institutions or organizations in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations that carry out protection duties, if they violate protection principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the mechanisms applicable within the internal institutions or respective organizations.

Article 39

1. Reporting on the implementation of protection for women and children from violence is carried out by:
a. P2TP2A to the Regent;
b. Task Force for the Protection of Women and Children at the Sub-District Level to the Sub-District Head; and

a. administration;
b. finance;
c. services; and
d. performance.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Garut Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Garut. 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of regional government administration. 5. Regency Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regency DPRD in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Regency region. 6. Protection is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and children victims of violence and discrimination starting from prevention efforts, services and social rehabilitation. 7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 8. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 9. Protection of Children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of freedom unlawfully. 11. Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 12. Violence against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 13. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development. 14. Domestic Violence hereinafter referred to as KDRT is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion, or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household. 15. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 16. Guardian is a person or body who in fact exercises parental authority as a Parent over a Child. 17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 18. Community is individuals, families, groups, and/or community organizations. 19. Non-Governmental Organization, hereinafter referred to as LSM, is an organization/institution formed by citizens of the Republic of Indonesia voluntarily of their own will and interested in and engaged in the field of social welfare business established by the organization/institution as a manifestation of community participation in efforts to improve community welfare that emphasizes voluntary service. 20. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs in the Garut Regency area. 21. Prevention is an effort to develop the capacity and mechanisms of the Regional Government and community in creating conditions that can prevent the occurrence of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation and/or neglect. 22. Handling is action that includes identification, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of women and children who are victims of acts of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation, maltreatment or neglect. 23. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 24. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing of the impending, ongoing or having occurred violence against victims. 25. Assistance is an effort made by a person or representative from an institution that has expertise in assisting victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 26. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society. 27. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out social functions properly. 28. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 29. Legal Aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to conduct the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender sensitive. 30.

Article 13

1. The community as referred to in Article 10 letter c has the obligation and responsibility for the protection of women and children through community participation activities in the protection of women and children.
2. Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), include:
a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or the competent authorities; and
c. participating in the handling of victims of acts of violence.

Article 11

1. The Regional Government as referred to in Article 10 letter a, is obliged and responsible to:
a. formulate and implement programs and activities related to the protection of women and children;
b. implement protection of women and children from violence;
c. supervise services to victims of violence based on minimum service standards in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations; and
d. allocate budget for protection of women and children from violence according to regional financial capacity.
2. In order to carry out the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regional Government formulates programs and activities for the protection of women and children in a regional action plan which is part of the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan

Article 36

1. The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector, NGOs/social organizations concerned with women and children in the protection of women and children against acts of violence.
2. The partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through:
a. notification of information on employment opportunities for women victims of violence;
b. education and training for women and children victims of violence;
c. educational assistance for women and children victims of violence who have been withdrawn from their education; and
d. fostering and enhancing the economic independence of women victims of violence.
3. The partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be set forth in the form of an agreement in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 12

1. The Village Government as referred to in Article 10 letter b, is obliged and responsible to:
a. formulate and implement programs and activities related to the protection of women and children;
b. implement protection of women and children from violence;
c. supervise services to victims of violence based on minimum service standards in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations; and
d. allocate budget for protection of women and children from violence according to village financial capacity.
2. In order to carry out the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in paragraph (1), the Village Government formulates programs and activities for the protection of women and children in a Village action plan which is part of the Village Medium-Term Development Plan (RPJMDes).

Article 7

1. Physical violence as referred to in Article 6 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death of women and/or children.
2. Psychological violence as referred to in Article 6 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering to women and/or children.
3. Sexual violence as referred to in Article 6 letter c, includes:
a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:
1\. physical harassment;
2\. verbal harassment;
3\. gestural harassment;
4\. written or pictorial harassment; and
5\. psychological/emotional harassment.
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/ord. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
4. Neglect as referred to in Article 6 letter d, includes:
a. acts that result in the failure to fulfill the needs of children properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after children as they should be, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/or
c. acts of deliberately neglecting women within their household sphere, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
5. Exploitation as referred to in Article 6 letter e, includes:
a. acts of economic or sexual exploitation with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the victim's consent which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or indecent acts.
6. Other violence as referred to in Article 6 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
7. Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
8. Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person/victim is made to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 3

The purpose of regulating the protection of women and children from acts of violence is to provide guidance and direction for the Regional Government and community in conducting prevention, services and social rehabilitation of women and child victims of acts of violence.
